A long slow swell runs the full length of the water, the whole surface rising at the near end and dropping at the far, each hull climbing at its own moment, out of step with the next.

A single soapsud crest stands three inches tall at the centre of the frame, thousands of tiny bubbles packed into its face, the topmost rank just tipping forward, each bubble separating from the mass and rolling down the front face alone.

Foam has broken into pack ice: irregular white rafts with lanes of clear cobalt water between them, each raft its own thickness, its own ragged edge, drifting slowly, a good gap of dark water between each.
Dead flat calm, the entire surface glass-still, a dark teal mirror so exact that each scuffed hull above has a twin below, both fleets sailing toward each other through a perfect join.
Chop has shattered the surface into a thousand angled facets, each one catching the surface at a different tilt, the water looking fractured, every facet tilted its own way.

Steam rolls low and dense across the water, thick enough that the far end of the fleet has gone, only the nearest hull still visible, the steam moving in slow separate masses that fold over each other.

The steam has torn into long ragged strips that travel across the surface at different speeds, one strip dissolving while the next behind it holds its shape, each gap between them showing clear dark water.
Near the drain, the water turns slowly, the surface dimpling down at the centre, loose foam spiralling inward in a long gradual curve, each bubble holding whole as it rides the rotation.

Three enormous bubbles, each the diameter of a large fist, stand clear above the general foam, their skins stretched thin and iridescent violet-gold, each one carrying a warped wide-angle reflection of the fleet curved across it.

A soap-film slick spreads outward from a point just off the port side of the nearest hull, the film carrying green and magenta interference colours that shift as it thins, the chop behind it going glassy wherever the slick reaches.

A crest at the weather end of the fleet tips over and throws spray as fifteen separate flung drops in the air at once, each one a sphere trailing a small tail, catching the surface and punching its own small ring as it lands.
A single drop lands on open water and throws a crown of eight separate upright spikes of water, each spike a different height, the outermost ring spreading outward as the crown collapses back.

A hundred drops arrive at once across the whole surface, each punching its own ring, the rings overlapping and crossing, the surface covered in intersecting circles expanding and flattening at different stages.

Foam covers the water from edge to edge in a thick continuous mass, individual bubbles visible across the top, each one its own pale sphere, only a fin and a funnel breaking through the surface of the mass.

The water is so still and clear that the bright enamel bottom is fully readable through it, every shadow of every hull lying sharp on that yellow bottom, the fleet doubled in the flat surface above and the shadows below.

Something has just come up through the surface: the water runs off it now in separate strings, each string finding its own path, each one thinning and breaking into drops before it reaches the flat water below.

Loose foam scraps cross the open water between the fleets, each scrap its own irregular shape, tumbling slowly end over end in the moving air just above the surface, none of them touching the water they cross.

A pale soap slick spreads forward from the bow of the nearest hull, thinning as it goes, the agitated chop ahead of it going progressively flatter as the slick passes over it, the boundary between rough and flat moving forward.

The water is lower than it was, and along the enamel at the far end a tide line is stranded: a broken ridge of collapsed foam running the width of the bath, each former bubble now a flat dry ring on the white enamel above the current surface.

Clear water from the tap end meets foam advancing from the drain end along a single ragged collision line, cobalt on one side, white on the other, the line itself moving slowly toward the tap as the foam gains.

The whole surface trembles in tiny rings too small to be spray, each ring appearing and vanishing in under a second, the rings densely spaced and arriving continuously as condensed steam drops back onto it.

A soapsud mountain range runs across the middle of the frame, peak and valley in clear succession, the peaks rounded and bright, the valleys between them darker and narrow, the whole range moving slowly broadside across the fleet's path.

The water leans hard: the far end has risen a full inch higher than the near end, the surface inclined, each hull sitting at the same angle as the water under it, the horizon line tilted across the frame.

A meniscus climbs each hull where the water meets rubber: a thin curved skin of soapy water creeping upward against gravity, holding for a moment at maximum reach, then pulling back in a slow retraction that leaves a damp line on the hull above the waterline.

Foam has packed into a continuous range of low rounded hills along the leeward edge, each hill built from hundreds of individual bubbles of slightly different sizes, the smallest ones at the crest already bursting one by one, leaving dark circular patches in the white mass.
